title: Mosques, Markets, and the KL Tower at Night
excerpt: I spent the day wandering Kuala Lumpur's historic core — nasi lemak at Central Market, two stunning mosques, and Merdeka Square — and stayed out late enough to watch the KL Tower glow against a moonlit sky.

photos.alt: Art Deco facade of Kuala Lumpur's Central Market (Pasar Seni), painted pale blue, with yellow Pasar Besar banners and the Malaysian flag flying above.
Looking up at the ornate star-shaped canopy over a pedestrian street near Central Market, KL, with colourful shophouses on either side.
Butik Batik Teraju stall inside Central Market, mannequins dressed in traditional batik garments and racks of brightly coloured sarongs on display.
A display plate of nasi lemak — coconut rice mounded on a blue plate with a boiled egg, peanuts, and sambal — labelled with a yellow sign reading 'Nasi Lemak (Creamy Coconut Milk Rice)'.
A person crouching on the green lawn of Dataran Merdeka (Independence Square), KL, with the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and the towering national flagpole behind them.
Masjid Jamek mosque viewed from across the river at dusk, its Moorish minarets and white domes framed by palm trees under a cloudy grey sky.
The slender modernist minaret of Masjid Negara (National Mosque) rising between two covered walkways, reflected in a rain-wet courtyard under an overcast sky.
Overhead shot of a dinner table: a plate of grilled sausages with roasted potatoes, a side salad, dark bread rolls in a basket, and a yellow tin drink can.
KL Tower lit up at night with red and green lights, its observation pod glowing teal, a full moon visible in the dark sky beside the shaft.
Illuminated floral fountain in front of Pavilion KL mall at night, with Louis Vuitton and Dior storefronts glowing behind a crowd of shoppers.
